name: Jollof Rice
description: Nigeria's most beloved dish — smoky, spiced tomato rice cooked to perfection with a signature party-style crust.

name: Egusi Soup
description: Rich, hearty soup made from ground melon seeds, leafy vegetables, and assorted meats in a palm oil base.

name: Suya
description: Spiced, skewered beef grilled over open flame and coated in a peanut-based yaji spice blend. A Lagos street food icon.

name: Pounded Yam
description: Smooth, stretchy pounded yam made from boiled yam tubers. Best served with egusi, okra, or banga soup.

name: Pepper Soup
description: A light, intensely spiced broth with catfish or goat meat, loaded with aromatic Nigerian spices and herbs.

name: Fried Plantain
description: Golden, caramelised slices of ripe plantain fried to a sweet, crispy perfection. A must-have side dish.

name: Ofada Rice & Stew
description: Locally grown unpolished rice served with a spicy, fermented locust bean stew loaded with assorted meats.

name: Moi Moi
description: Steamed bean pudding made from blended black-eyed peas, peppers, and onions. Soft, savoury, and nutritious.

name: Banga Soup
description: A rich Delta-style palm nut soup with aromatic spices, dried fish, and assorted meats. Deep, complex flavour.

name: Akara
description: Crispy, deep-fried bean cakes made from blended black-eyed peas and peppers. A classic Lagos breakfast staple.

name: Ofe Onugbu
description: Bitter leaf soup from Eastern Nigeria, cooked with cocoyam, palm oil, and assorted proteins. Bold and earthy.

name: Nkwobi
description: Spiced cow foot cooked in a rich palm oil and ugba sauce. A popular evening delicacy in Lagos restaurants.

name: Eba & Okra Soup
description: Garri-based swallow served with silky, draw okra soup loaded with fish and crayfish. A Nigerian comfort meal.

name: Chapman
description: Nigeria's favourite cocktail — a refreshing blend of Fanta, Sprite, Ribena, cucumber, and Angostura bitters.

name: Chin Chin
description: Crunchy, deep-fried dough snacks seasoned with nutmeg and sugar. A beloved Nigerian party and everyday snack.

name: Asun
description: Smoky, peppered goat meat grilled and tossed with scotch bonnet peppers and onions. A party favourite.
